mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy stance, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months, or if the correlation between RSAFS changes and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 9% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a severe economic downturn with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate fiscal stimulus and policy support.
regime_hint: severe economic downturn with accommodative policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9% and FEDFUNDS < 1%, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and FEDFUNDS on S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% in a quarter and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in 1 quarter and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 2% and FEDFUNDS is above 2%, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.
